scope: Read all 16 selected texts in full with their stored historical-proxy, extraction, date and attribution evidence. Descriptions reflect observed prose, not source-name or prompt-profile labels. No fresh historical archive or underlying factual audit.
aggregate_findings: The fixed Train sample already includes promotional suspense questions, plain and evaluative plot narration, repetitive technical definitions, specialist abstracts and source defects. This establishes presence of these examples, not adequate coverage or learned robustness.

Three sampled research abstracts use first-person plural researcher actions; none of the 16 is a personal letter or diary. The sample cannot establish that those registers are absent from all 471 human roots.

The selected news digest contains eight headline/dateline/excerpt units and editorial status labels. A collection label and page ID do not by themselves establish one coherent article or one underlying source work.

All 16 carry historical_proxy evidence. The PLOS records additionally say historical byte identity is unverified. Wikipedia/Wikinews revisions offer stronger version references but still do not document human-only authorship.

supplemental_context_review.judgment: The second digest explicitly presents an article index with navigation, datelines and excerpts. Its 12-word normalized match is the same Ukrainian-opposition headline. The following excerpts concern different reported actions and dates. This is shared headline text between two Train compilations, not evidence of cross-split contamination or a basis for automatic family merging.

next_interpretation: Finish and inspect all six saved-artifact Train-fit runs before choosing a training intervention. This reading does not establish whether A fitted these examples or which textual properties caused Test errors.
